topic: Hono API on Cloudflare Workers + D1 via Drizzle ORM (2026 best practices)

notes: Hono v5 exists only on the 'next' dist-tag (5.0.0-rc.1). Pin ^4.13.20 for stability.

drizzle-orm/drizzle-kit v1 is on 'rc' dist-tag and the official docs now write installs as `drizzle-orm@rc` / `drizzle-kit@rc`. Latest STABLE is 0.45.4 / 0.31.11. v1 changes the on-disk migration layout (nested dirs) which affects D1 config.

@cloudflare/workers-types is now date-versioned major 5.x. Cloudflare increasingly prefers generated types via `wrangler types` (worker-configuration.d.ts) over hand-pinned workers-types; keep workers-types only if you want the ambient global types.

config_snippets.drizzle_schema_src_db_schema_ts:
import { sqliteTable, integer, text, real } from 'drizzle-orm/sqlite-core'

export const runs = sqliteTable('runs', {
  id: integer('id').primaryKey({ autoIncrement: true }),
  userId: text('user_id').notNull(),
  distanceKm: real('distance_km').notNull(),
  durationSec: integer('duration_sec').notNull(),
  notes: text('notes'),
  createdAt: integer('created_at', { mode: 'timestamp' }).notNull().defaultNow()
})

tsconfig_alternative_generated_types.note: Preferred by Cloudflare: run `wrangler types` to emit worker-configuration.d.ts and use `types: []` from tsconfig, then type Hono as new Hono<{ Bindings: CloudflareBindings }>(). Drop @cloudflare/workers-types to avoid duplicate/conflicting global type declarations.

commands: npm create hono@latest strideguide-api   # choose the 'cloudflare-workers' template
npx wrangler d1 create strideguide-db    # prints database_id to paste into wrangler.jsonc
npx wrangler types --env-interface CloudflareBindings   # generate worker-configuration.d.ts
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply strideguide-db --local    # apply to local D1 (.wrangler/state)
npx wrangler dev                          # local server on http://127.0.0.1:8787
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply strideguide-db --remote   # apply to production D1
ALTERNATIVE single-step REMOTE migrate without wrangler: npx drizzle-kit migrate   # needs driver:'d1-http' + CLOUDFLARE_* env vars
npx drizzle-kit studio                    # optional GUI (needs d1-http creds for remote)
gotchas: Migration layout changed in the v1 RC line: `drizzle-kit generate` now writes NESTED dirs, e.g. drizzle/20261122125510_init/migration.sql + snapshot.json. Older drizzle-kit wrote flat drizzle/0000_name.sql. Cloudflare's wrangler default glob is `migrations/*.sql`, which MISSES the nested layout, so set `migrations_pattern: "drizzle/*/migration.sql"` (must be prefixed by migrations_dir, and both must be set).

Because of the nested layout, `wrangler d1 migrations create` is not usable for Drizzle projects (it only writes top-level files). Always author migrations with `drizzle-kit generate` (or `generate --custom` for hand-written SQL).

Two different migration ledgers exist and must not be mixed on the same DB: wrangler records applied files in `d1_migrations`; drizzle-kit migrate records in `__drizzle_migrations`. Pick ONE path per database. Recommended for D1: `drizzle-kit generate` + `wrangler d1 migrations apply`. Only use `drizzle-kit migrate` if you deliberately skip wrangler.

`wrangler d1 migrations apply|execute|list|export` now expect an explicit `--local` or `--remote` flag; without it wrangler prompts (and CI/non-interactive runs behave differently). Always pass the flag explicitly in scripts.

drizzle-kit needs the flat `breakpoints: true` (default) so generated SQL contains `--> statement-breakpoint` separators; SQLite/D1 cannot run multiple DDL statements in one transaction. Do not disable breakpoints for D1.

D1 local data is persisted by default under `.wrangler/state/v3/d1`. Change the location with `wrangler dev --persist-to=...`; the same dir is used by `wrangler d1 migrations apply --local` (pass `--persist-to` to both to keep them in sync).
Workers AI has no local simulation and ALWAYS runs remotely. Set `"ai": { "binding": "AI", "remote": true }`; omitting `remote` logs a warning and `remote: false` is an ERROR.

`.dev.vars` (dotenv syntax) supplies local secrets/vars for `wrangler dev` and is auto-loaded; it is NOT uploaded. Production secrets need `wrangler secret put <NAME>` (or dashboard). `process.env` is unavailable unless you enable the `nodejs_compat_populate_process_env` flag; read config via `c.env` in Hono.

Cron Triggers: `triggers.crons` drives the `scheduled(controller, env, ctx)` export and runs on UTC using 5-field, Quartz-style expressions (weekday 1=Sun..7=Sat). To disable, set `crons: []`; commenting it out leaves deployed crons in place. Test locally with `curl 'http://localhost:8787/cdn-cgi/local/scheduled?cron=*+*+*+*+*'`.
Keep D1 binding name stable but prefer the DATABASE NAME for `wrangler d1 ...` commands (binding names can be renamed; DB names cannot) to avoid migrating the wrong database.
Set `compatibility_date` to a recent date (e.g. today) and only add `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]` if a dependency needs Node built-ins; Hono + Drizzle do not require it.

Drizzle with D1 driver: use `drizzle-orm/d1` (takes the raw `D1Database` binding). Prefer `.all()`/`.get()`/`.run()`/`.values()`-style returns and note D1 has no interactive transactions — use `db.batch([...])` for atomic multi-statement writes.

Hono's built-in `Env` type name collides with Cloudflare's generated `Env` interface — pass `--env-interface CloudflareBindings` to `wrangler types` and use `new Hono<{ Bindings: CloudflareBindings }>()`.

Hono v5 is only on the `next` tag; and Drizzle v1 is only on `rc`. Pin stable (`hono@^4.13.20`, `drizzle-orm@^0.45.4`, `drizzle-kit@^0.31.11`) unless you explicitly want the RCs; if you take Drizzle v1, adopt the nested migrations layout consistently.
